episodes.172382: An upper level short wave moving overhead combined with a surface pressure trough to enhance isolated thunderstorm development across the central and southern South Plains. Although instability values were not very high, they were able to create robust enough updrafts to generate severe size hail as well as severe downburst winds. Brownfield (Terry County) saw brief torrential rainfall along with hail up to quarter size that covered the ground.
episodes.172668: A 13 year-old boy and an 11 year-old boy were killed when lightning struck or nearly struck the crew boat that they were in, causing it to capsize on Lake Fairview in Orange County. Three other boys were able to make it to shore and survived.
episodes.172849: An upper level trough had moved into the Central Plains. An upper level disturbance associated with the upper trough moved over West Texas. This helped increase lift over the area. Low-level moisture was also fairly high across the area. These conditions resulted in storms that produced severe wind gusts and flash flooding across parts of West Texas.
episodes.173034: Debris occurred over State Highway 376 from mile markers 68 to 72 along with water running over the roadway. NDOT closed the highway. Depth of debris appears to be several inches from photo.
episodes.173216: Marginally-severe thunderstorms affected Gosper and Furnas counties during the evening hours of September 15th. A weak upper level shortwave along with a surface trough combined with moderate instability and abundant moisture to spark off clusters of thunderstorms during the late afternoon and early evening hours. The strongest storms impacted portions of Gosper and Furnas Counties between 6-8 PM CDT, with localized instances of penny to nickel size hail reported. A lone severe wind gust of 65 MPH was also reported. While instability was moderate and moisture was plentiful, weak deep layer wind shear of only 20 knots or less likely precluded a greater, or more widespread, severe weather threat. Scattered to widespread showers and thunderstorms continued well into the late evening hours, but thunderstorm intensity greatly decreased with loss of daytime heating.
episodes.173295: A stalled frontal boundary extended across NE FL, with heavy rainfall south of the front in convergent bands that moved onshore and extended inland from roughly St. Augustine southward toward Gainesville.
episodes.173695: An active pattern in mid-September resulted in several reports of flash flooding in southern Utah, in addition to some isolated thunderstorm related wind gusts in northern Utah.
episodes.174050: A trough of low pressure pushed northeastward across northern Arizona with isolated thunderstorms and heavy rain.
episodes.174245: Slow moving storms brought heavy rain to the Cedar Creek Burn Scar area creating a debris flow across Highway 20. Observations in the near the site in Mazama showed rain amounts half an inch in hour and three quarters of inch in 24 hours.
episodes.174339: Pockets of showers and thunderstorms developed across northeastern South Dakota as an area of low pressure tracked northeast during the overnight of the 14th into the 15th. These thunderstorms produced isolated severe thunderstorm wind gusts around 60 mph at the Summit and Peever SDDOT stations, and also damaged trees on the northwest side of Aberdeen.
episodes.174434: An upper level shortwave trough moved east-northeast through southeast Colorado and northeast New Mexico during the afternoon and evening hours.  Isolated severe thunderstorms developed in the southern and northeast Texas Panhandle.  Shear and instability were weak.  Thunderstorms were generally unorganized and formed in clusters.  A thunderstorm that developed over northwest Amarillo moved east and collided with a westward moving outflow boundary.  This caused the thunderstorm to intensify.  The storm produced golf ball size hail and half dollar size hail to the east of Amarillo.  Two outflow boundaries collided to the southeast of Amarillo causing a brief landspout.  A severe wind gust was recorded west of Lipscomb from an isolated severe storm.
episodes.174574: A weak short wave trough moved across a marginally unstable atmosphere.  A weak surface boundary and lifting from the weak short waved helped to initiate a few severe thunderstorms.

events.narrative: Heavy rain resulted in flash flooding in the City of Midland. There were multiple stalled vehicles reported in flash flooding at the intersections of North Loop 250 and Lancashire, North Garfield and Castleford, and Midland Drive and Wadley. The cost of damage is a very rough estimate.
Havasu Creek rose two feet in 15 minuets just above the Village of Supai.

Heavy rain over the Cedar Creek Burn Scar caused a debris flow over Highway 20 near Mazama. Observations in the near the site in Mazama showed precip amounts half an inch in hour and three quarters of inch in 24 hours.
Debris occurred over State Highway 376 from mile markers 68 to 72 along with water running over the roadway. NDOT closed the highway. Depth of debris appears to be several inches from photo.

Heavy rain resulted in flash flooding in north Odessa. There was a road closure at the intersection of Andrews Highway and 87th Street in north Odessa due to flooding. The cost of damage is a very rough estimate.
A mesonet station AV639 about 5 miles SW of the Ocala Airport measured 2.29 inches of rainfall.

The Brown County Emergency Manager reported damage around the fairgrounds, and a social media report with photos depicted tree damage at Rolling Meadows Drive, both on the north side of Aberdeen. The time of the damage is radar estimated.
The WeatherStem mesonet at the Haw Creek Community Center measured 3.68 inches of rainfall between 1:20 pm and 2:30 pm.
A mesonet site via the WunderMap interface measured 3.13 inches of rainfall between 2 pm and 6 pm.

Bureau of Land Management officials reported a flash flood wave moving down Phipps Wash toward the Escalante River. This is most likely associated with a brief thunderstorm which moved through the area between roughly 11:30 am MST to 12:30 pm MST and produced moderate to heavy rainfall. Event time is based upon report.
A personal weather station at Beulah Church in Fruitland measured 2.19 inches of rainfall in about 1 hour.

Park rangers relayed a report of flash flooding in Capitol Gorge, with floodwaters as much as 4 feet deep. This is associated with showers and thunderstorms which moved through the area between around 12:30 pm MST to 2:00 pm MST and produced around 0.50 inches of rainfall.

The Orlando Fire Department and local news media reported that a crew boat with five boys was struck or nearly struck by lightning, causing the boat to capsize, at around 1615LST. Four of the boys made it to shore, where one was sent to the hospital. The fifth boy was missing for a time and was later found deceased. The hospitalized boy was in critical condition and was declared brain dead. He was taken off of life support a few days later.
An NWS cooperative weather observer reported quarter size hail in Brownfield.
A Texas Tech University West Texas mesonet site near Brownfield measured a wind gust of 58 mph.
